tossups.text: One piece of evidence that supports its existence is that the Caledonian mountains of Northern Europe are a continuation of the Appalachian Mountains. This entity broke up into Laurasia and Gondwanaland ("gon-DWON-uh-land"). Alfred Wegener ("VAY-guh-nuhr") coined its name during a lecture in which he discussed his theory of continental drift. For 10 points, identify this supercontinent theorized to have existed 250 million years ago.

In this play, one character mistakenly calls another character Egeria, adding that this was "a classical allusion merely". One character in this play remarks that "the truth is rarely pure and never simple", while another notes that "to lose one parent may be regarded as a misfortune; to lose both looks like carelessness". Canon Chasuble appears in this play, in which a handbag discovered at Victoria Station is famously discussed by Aunt Augusta. For 10 points, name this Oscar Wilde play in which Algernon goes 'Bunburying' in order to avoid his social obligations.

This psychologist recorded his personal struggles with psychosis in his "Red Book," which was not published until 2009. This psychologist proposed a principle principle that events linked in meaning need not share causes, which he dubbed "synchronicity." He also theorized about an unconscious male type called the animus and a female type called the anima, which are examples of his archetypes. For 10 points, name this Swiss Psychologist who developed the idea of the collective unconscious.

Ezra Pound's second Canto begins by telling this man to "hang it all", as "there can be but one 'Sordello!'" He wrote "Grow old along with me! The best is yet to be" in a poem appearing in his collection Dramatis Personae, and in addition to "Rabbi ben Ezra," he wrote a work in which the narrator used "one long yellow string" of his lover's hair to strangle her. This author of "Porphyria's Lover" more famously wrote a poem in which the narrator's "nine-hundred-years old name" was ranked "with anybody's gift" by a woman with "a heart too soon made glad" painted by Fra Pandolf. For 10 points, name this English poet of dramatic monologues including "My Last Duchess."

Chairlike transition states were posited to determine E/Z selectivity in the formation of these molecules in the Ireland model. In the the alkylation of these nucleophilic molecules, clustered ones tend to react at the softer reaction center, resulting in C-alklyation. Strong bases, such as LDA, catalyze the formation of kinetic ones, while weaker bases promote the formation of thermodynamic ones, and sufficiently weak bases can allow this charged intermediate to react with the compound from which it is generated--this reaction is called a crossed aldol reaction. This compound is generated when a strong base abstracts an alpha hydrogen in the first step of the Michael addition. For 10 points, name this class of reactive compounds, the conjugate bases of carbonyl compounds, which can be formed by deprotonating the tautomer of a keto compound.

Creations of this type include Roland Barthes's (BART'S) "Death of the Author." Supporting details and examples are found in body paragraphs in this type of writing, genres of which include process, descriptive, argumentative, and compare-and-contrast. A five-paragraph type of these is frequently assigned in high schools. For 10 points, name this type of non-fiction writing that seeks to prove a thesis statement.

Before adopting a liberal abortion position, this politician claimed that abortion was murder and "could have killed Moses and Jesus" during a presidential campaign. This politician boosted his domestic profile with the 1983 release Robert Goodman's release by Hafez al-Assad and the 1984 release of twenty-two Americans by Fidel Castro, helping him win third place in primaries behind Gary Hart and Walter Mondale. Protests against this politician's suspension from the SCLC were organized by Al Sharpton.This man, who organized People United to Save Humanity, or PUSH, has a son of the same name was convicted on accounts of wire and mail fraud, leading him to resign as an Illinois congressman and serve 30 months in federal prison. This man's failed 1988 campaign for president aimed to mobilize a "Rainbow Coalition" of minorities and progressives. For 10 points, name this civil rights activist and Baptist minister.

A street in this city that divided its poor and rich sections was nicknamed "the Slot." Amadeo Giannini's Bank of Italy, which grew into the Bank of America, was founded in this city. Mayor Eugene Schmitz, the puppet of Union Labor Party boss Abe Ruef, created the Committee of Fifty to respond to a disaster in this city. This city exhibited its recovery from that disaster by hosting the extravagant 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition. A fire in this city destroyed many opulent Nob Hill mansions. Around 80% of this city was destroyed in a fire that started after its 1906 earthquake. For 10 points, name this city that is the southern terminus of the Golden Gate Bridge.

Lennard Davis coined a portmanteau that pairs this concept with postmodernism to argue for a mode of thinking organized around "dependency and interdependence." In Frontiers of Justice, Martha Nussbaum argues that John Rawls's contractarianism is unable to fully account for this concept. A book by Rosemarie Garland-Thomson contrasts this concept with that of the "normate." Advocates of "people-first language" argue that it works to prevent this concept from defining individuals. In the United States, the IDEA ("I-D-E-A") requires people described by this term to be educated in the "least restrictive environment," a practice also known as "mainstreaming." A 1990 law requires employers to provide "reasonable accommodations" for Americans described by this term. For 10 points, name this term that refers to the restrictions experienced by people with conditions such as paraplegia and blindness.
acceptableAnswers: accept dismodernism and more specific answers that mention disability
prompt on descriptive terms such as impairment and handicapped
and specific examples such as blindness

tossups.text: Mass movements of this kind of matter in the atmosphere can result in Birkeland currents. Tension on magnetic field lines results in low-frequency oscillations in this matter called Alfven waves. This matter is treated like a fluid in the field of magnetohydrodynamics, and a magnetic field is used to confine this kind of matter in the shape of a torus in a tokamak (TOW-kuh-mak). Auroras are an example of this matter, whose partially ionized form makes up lightning. For 10 points, name this "fourth state of matter" that comprises the Sun.

The power of magistrates in this colony was contested in a dispute involving a militia in the town of Hingham. Though many of this colony's initial settlers travelled on the Arbella, its longest-serving governor John Endecott didn't. Another leader of this colony declared that "the eyes of all people are upon us" in his sermon "A Model of Christian Charity," which describes this colony as a "city upon a hill." John Winthrop helped found this colony, which expelled Anne Hutchinson and merged with a separate settlement founded by the passengers of the Mayflower. For 10 points, Plymouth was absorbed by what New England colony that names a modern-day state?

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for cortisol functions. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this adrenal-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The adrenal is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in cortisol functions.

tossups.text: This man proposed a glass and steel design for the Friedrichstrasse Office Building but his idea was rejected. In one building, this architect specified window blinds which could only be set as open, closed, or halfway closed. This architect used bronze-toned steel beams to suggest structure in that building. He collaborated with Lilly Reich to produce a leather and chrome chair for the German pavilion at the Barcelona exposition. This architect of the Farnsworth House and the Seagram Building was known for his maxims "God is in the detail" and "Less is more". For 10 points, name this German-American architect final director of the Bauhaus.

Two figures on the left of this paining are derived from a Holbein print of gamblers unaware of Death. A sword is hanging from the belt of a figure sitting at a table who faces backward, while the figures on the left wear contemporary garb and the two men on the right wear cloaks. This painting features three sources of light including an oilskin-covered window, as well as a bearded figure whose left hand is pointing at his own chest while his right hand is on a coin. This painting is found alongside two works about the "inspiration" and "martyrdom" of the title figure in the Contarelli Chapel. Depicting a man formerly known as Levi, for 10 points, name this painting in which Jesus summons a tax collector, by Caravaggio.

Mixtures containing this compound and proteins with aromatic rings turn yellow upon heating, an observation used in the xanthoproteic test. This substance, which comes in red fuming and white fuming varieties, can be used to synthesize aniline by addition followed by reduction. One inefficient process for producing this compound using an electrical arc was named for Birkeland and Eyde, but a more widely used process makes use of a platinum-rhodium catalyst. That process provides raw material for the production of fertilizer and is named for Ostwald. This compound is found along with hydrochloric acid in a mixture that can dissolve gold. For 10 points, name this compound found in aqua regia, a strong acid with formula HNO3.

It is listed as NGC 224 and was observed by Abd al-Sufi in 964, although Simon Marius was credited as its discoverer for a time. It is one of the few blue shifted entities of its type, meaning that it is approaching the earth and will collide with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years. With an apparent magnitude of 3.4, it is one of the brightest objects in the Messier Catalogue, where it is listed as M31. While it has probably about the same mass as the Milky Way, it is much larger, making it the largest member of the local group. For ten points, name this galaxy, the nearest spiral galaxy to the Milky Way.

The "Salt Pan" is a section of the Cienaga de Zapatas Park, which is located in its Matanzas province. The longest river in this country partly forms the border between the Holguin and Granma provinces after originating in the Sierra Maestra, and the chain of islands extending from its Hicasos peninsula to the Nuevitas bay is called the Sabana-Camaguey archipelago. Isla de la Juventud is located south of the Gulf of Batabano off the Caribbean coast of this country, whose cities include Pinar del Rio and Santiago. Located south of the Straits of Florida, for 10 points, identify this country whose easternmost province is Guantanamo and whose capital is Havana.

One of this structure is required for the formation of a protocorm. That structure is present as a peloton in orchid embryos and is required for the seeds to germinate. Another type of this is present between cortical cells as Hartig nets. The formation of specialized lateral roots, or 'hair roots', occurs due to the ericoid type. The Monotropoid type forms a bridge between plants of the family Monotropaceae and conifers. The most common type of this, arbuscular, is named for its finely branched clusters of hyphae which are the main site of nutrient exchange. For 10 points, name this symbiotic relationship between a fungus and the roots of a vascular plant.

Also known as the "Nizaris," their most important fortress was called Alamut. The Syrian branch was eventually subjugated by Baybars, while Hulagu Khan destroyed their Persian sect. Led by a man known as "the Old Man of the Mountain," one of their most prominent enemiess was the vizier of Malik Shah, Nizam al-Mulk. They were organized by Hassan al-Shabbah into strict classes, the most important of which were the "devotees" who were treated to nights of great pleasure. Fo 10 points, identify this secret sect of opiate-abusing Ismaili warriors and masterful killers, whose name is now used to identify politically motivated murderers.

This character orders actors to perform The Murder of Gonzago , a play-within-a-play, in order to prove his uncle's guilt. This character mistakenly stabs Polonius through a curtain, believing him to be King Claudius. This character's lover, Ophelia, drowns after falling from a willow tree. For ten points, name this Prince of Denmark who says "To be, or not to be" in a famous soliloquy of the Shakespearean play he titles.

parts.text: Soldiers were burned in World War I when this gas, containing impure sulfur, was dropped from planes. Its yellow-brown color gave this substance its name.
The first poison gas deployed in World War I consisted of this gaseous element. In small quantities, this element can be used to disinfect water supplies.
This organophosphorus nerve agent causes a rapid loss in muscle function and was infamously used in a Tokyo subway attack in 1995.

parts.text: This Stevens poem about a title ruler begins, "Call the roller of big cigars, / The muscular one, and bid him whip / In kitchen cups concupiscient curds."

"Thirteen Ways of Looking at a Blackbird" and "The Emperor of Ice Cream" first appeared in this Stevens collection that was originally published in 1923. It also included "Peter Quince at the Clavier" and "Domination of Black".

parts.text: Name this property of words whose grammatical number is greater than the singular.
The plural of "octopus" is "octopodes" as a result of it being a word derived from this language, whose alphabet includes letters such as alpha and beta.
In Swahili, the plural of "kitabu" is "vitabu," a result of it being one of these words taken from another language.

parts.text: Name this poet of "Archaic Torso of Apollo", whose published collections include Duino Elegies and Sonnets to Orpheus.
Rilke wrote in this language, which was also used by Bertolt Brecht and Herman Hesse.
Another famous Rilke poem is about this type of feline, described as having "powerful soft strides." This type of cat is also the subject of an Ambrose Bierce short story.

parts.text: Sandhoff disease results from mutation of the beta subunit of which protein, coded for by chromosome 15, whose normal hydrolysis of Gm2 gangliosides is disrupted in Tay-Sachs disease.

Mutations of the HEXA gene thus explain Tay-Sachs as one of the "storage disorders" in which the function of this organelle is impaired. Gaucher's and Neiman-Pick diseases similarly impair this digestive organelle.

Chromosome 15 is also the site of the UBE3A deletion that afflicts this disease's laughter-prone victims, whose frequent depiction by hack renaissance painters earned in the nickname "Happy Puppet Syndrome." It is a classic illustration of genetic imprinting along with a similar disease that effects paternal genes, Prader-Willi syndrome.

bonuses.leadin: The insertion of a TATC stop codon is the most common mutation associated with this enzyme, which is structurally similar to NCOAT and functions via an arginine-424 residue. FTPE:

parts.text: Name this last name shared by a founder of Pragmatism named John and a developer of a library classification system named Melvil.
John Dewey developed Pragmatism with William James, who taught at Harvard University in this state. James's brother Henry wrote The Bostonians, which is set in this state.
This earlier American Transcendentalist philosopher wrote about his stay at Walden Pond in Massachusetts, where he also wrote "Civil Disobedience."

bonuses.leadin: A philosopher with this last name developed experimental education in his Democracy and Education. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Isaias Afwerki's Eritrea is nicknamed "Africa's" version of what longtime ally of Uganda? It funded Juche ("JOO-chay") study groups across Africa.

Many Windhoek ("wind-hook") landmarks were built by this North Korean art studio, which created memorials to Agostinho Neto ("ah-gose-CHEEN-yo NEH-too"), Samora Machel ("mah-SHELL"), and Derg soldiers, as well as Dakar's African Renaissance Monument.

Mansudae built the National Heroes Acre, which inters many perpetrators of this genocide. North Korea trained the Fifth Brigade that led this genocide of the Ndebele ("un-day-BEH-lay") for Robert Mugabe's ZANU ("ZAH-noo") in Bhalagwe ("buh-LAH-gway").

parts.text: Name these people, the subject of Alonso de Ercilla's Araucania. A modern group of this indigenous people were forced to relocate from their home along the Bio-Bio River by the Ralco dam.
The Mapuche are the largest indigenous group in this country. The Yaghan people of Tierra del Fuego live in both this country and its eastern neighbor.

Discovery of the Monte Verde archaeological site in Chile, the oldest in the Americas, lent credence to the theory that the first settlers of the Americas used this method to arrive, as opposed to walking over the Bering Land Bridge.
acceptableAnswers: answers that indicate sailing along the coast

parts.text: Name this animal that was taboo in many Eurasian cultures. However, either the original Proto-Indo-European name for this animal or a very early taboo replacement is likely preserved in its Latin name Ursus.
That phenomenon makes the word for bear a term described by this originally Māori ("MAH-or-ee") word, the opposite of taboo.
The bear taboo of Proto-Indo-Europeans may have come about through contact with speakers of this language family. This language family includes Estonian and the Sámi languages.

bonuses.leadin: A taboo against the name of this animal led to its English name being derived either from a word for wild animal or for brown. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This object designated Messier 1 was used to measure the thickness of Titan's atmosphere as the moon made a transit of it. This nebula is located in the constellation Taurus.
This nearby spiral galaxy is designated Messier 31. It is the largest galaxy in the local group.
Messier 87 is the elliptical galaxy located at the center of this supercluster that includes the local group.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each name these Messier Objects.

parts.text: Name this ancient Greek city state in the Peloponnese which put a huge emphasis on military power and made all citizens undergo the agoge training regimen.
Sparta traced its heritage back to this legendary lawgiver, who emphasized the virtues of equality, austerity, and military fitness.
Only the firstborn sons of the royal families were exempted from the agoge. Name either royal family.

What is the main function of the epidermis in the integumentary system?
Name another component of the integumentary system related to skin cell types.

parts.text: Identify this artistic movement whose most famous representative was Piet Mondrian.
This man founded the Stijl movement, and eventually broke away from it with a variant he named "elementarism." Mondrian was so pissed he quit the group.
This 1924 building, designed by Gerrit Rietveld, is representative of de Stijl architecture, and is notable for its emphasis on primary colors and straight lines.

bonuses.leadin: Gerrit Rietveld and J.J.P. Oud were its architectural representatives. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this contemporary composer, who won the 2001 Pulitzer for his second symphony. His first symphony was inspired by the AIDS crisis, and he adapted a violin concerto for Joshua Bell from his score for the film The Red Violin.

Pierre de Beaumarchais tries to appease the ghost of Marie Antoinette in this only opera by John Corigliano, in which Figaro causes mischief from an opera within the opera and tries to save Marie from her beheading.
Stanley Drucker premiered Corigliano's popular 1977 concerto for this woodwind instrument. Aaron Copland's jazz-influenced concerto for this instrument was commissioned by Benny Goodman.

bonuses.leadin: This composer's oboe concerto begins with a playful "tuning game," which confuses many audience members into thinking the piece has not yet begun. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this type of path which is traced out by an inertial test particle in free fall according to general relativity.

The geodesic equation includes this man's namesake symbols, which can be expressed in terms of the metric and its coordinate derivatives. He also lends his name, with Schwarz, to a conformal mapping used in potential flow problems in fluid dynamics.

This curvature tensor is a contraction of the Riemann tensor that can be expressed in terms of the Christoffel symbols; it relates the size of a volume element in a manifold to its size in Euclidean space. Its namesake flow was used to prove the Poincaré conjecture.

bonuses.leadin: These paths are the shortest route between two points on curved spaces; for a sphere they correspond to great circles. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this physicist that names those "A" and "B" coefficients important in the study of blackbody radiation.
Einstein is most famous for his work on special relativity, in which he proposed that E is equal to m times this quantity squared.
Einstein won the Nobel for his explanation of this effect. In it, electrons are ejected from light shot at a metal surface with an energy equal to the photon energy minus a "work function."

parts.text: This country is a popular diving destination since it hosts the second largest barrier reef in the world. The Great Blue Hole is surrounded by the Lighthouse Reef atoll off of this country's coast.
Divers in the Caribbean often visit these structures. The Bermuda Triangle is believed to have many of these structures due to sailors getting lost within it.
Some of the world's most popular shore diving sites are off the coast of Bonaire, Curaçao, and this third island in the Dutch-owned ABC islands. This island's capital is Oranjestad.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about popular diving locations in the Caribbean Sea, for 10 points each.

parts.text: The signal is produced when a positron, a particle of this class, is created by lightning and then annihilates with an electron. Particles of this class are generally the same as ordinary particles but have opposite charges.

For a particle and its antiparticle to be distinct, they must be excitations of a field with this property. When quantizing a scalar field with this mathematical property, the Fourier coefficients for positive and negative frequencies become distinct creation and annihilation operators.

The photons that Fermi detects are their own antiparticles. This neutral, massive Standard Model boson is also its own antiparticle, but, unlike the photon, it is unstable and mediates the weak force.

bonuses.leadin: The Fermi Gamma-Ray telescope sometimes sees thunderstorms output gamma radiation at 511 kiloelectronvolts. Answer the following about this phenomenon, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this state, in which the Star of the West was fired upon by Confederate forces during a siege in which Robert Anderson surrendered to P.G.T. Beauregard.
Beauregard besieged Fort Sumter, which is located in this South Carolinian port city, the most populous in South Carolina.
This ship pilot and escaped slave hijacked the CSS Planter in Charleston harbor, and would later represent South Carolina in the US Senate.

bonuses.leadin: Gullah-speaking slaves in this state were granted land in the Port Royal Experiment. For ten points each:

parts.text: This Old English epic poem's title character, a king of the Geats, helps defend the mead hall of King Hrothgar against the monster Grendel.
One of King Arthur's knights competes in a "beheading game" with Bertilek, who returns to finish it a year and a day after having his head cut off, in this Middle English story.

parts.text: Both Beowulf and Sir Gawain and the Green Knight are written in a style of poetry that uses this device rather than rhyme. "Big beautiful blue berries" is an example of this device, in which authors use many words that begin with the same sound or letter.
